label: Schertz 1699 Moravian arms: one given Wappen explained through history and heraldic art

features.value: the current arms of the Margraviate of Moravia are explicitly declared the target of the description
historical writers, political change and heraldic doctrine are mobilised around explaining one territorial coat of arms
author states that access to rare Moravian manuscripts in major libraries would have enabled a more fully worked study
earlier historians and heraldic descriptions are compared, supplemented or criticised rather than merely cited

sources.citation: Carl Ferdinand von Schertz, Mährisches Landes-Wapen Aus der Histori Und Herolds-Kunst Illuminiret (Nürnberg: Zieger, 1699), 42 pp.
Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek, Carl Ferdinand von Schertz, works include Mährisches Landes-Wappen
Moravská orlice, Schertz 1699 long German transcription; reports BSB, SLUB and Austrian National Library digital witnesses

notes: Direct bibliographic controls are secure; detailed method claims currently depend on the modern long transcription and require page-level collation against an institutional scan before promotion to verified_primary. Use as a pre-Gatterer comparator, not as evidence of direct influence.

label: Working comparator: broad heraldic compendium versus object-centred historical-heraldic monograph

relations.note: Gatterer's later negative Rudolphi judgment provides the methodological boundary; Schertz offers an earlier short, object-centred comparator in the same Nürnberg print environment.

features.value: Rudolphi's broad source-rich compendium can later be classified as blazonist, whereas Schertz concentrates historical materials around one particular Wappen

notes: Comparative heuristic only. No Schertz→Gatterer or Schertz→Rudolphi influence chain is established.
